uzo.purpose: Tells the person in the flow of the page what happened or what to watch for: saved, could not save, import not confirmed.

instead.kialo: A notice asks nothing, because it reads in the flow of the page; what needs a decision interrupts, and that is a dialogo.
One to three words next to a title are a badge, because a status is read at a glance; a notice is a sentence.
An error of one field stands at the field, because the person corrects it there (slot error of the kampo); a notice names what no field owns.

boundary.kialo: A notice that goes away by itself is not readable for everyone, because some read slowly or look later; an Ero with a time rule is its own.
Several notices at once compete for the same attention, because each claims the flow of the page; a person decides which stay and in which order.

containers.name: page
containers.kialo: A notice belongs to the page whose state it tells, because that is where the person reads on.

containers.name: dialog
containers.kialo: A notice stands at the top of a dialog's content when a confirmation failed, because the person decides there what to do next.

with.kialo: A notice may offer the next step as an action, because what to do about it is one button: at most one with emphasis high.
A notice may lead to where the matter is, because a destination is a link, not an action.
The icon of the intent stands before the words as an ikono, because a sign is read faster than a word; never alone — the intent word is heard, the colour is the status text's (G6).
A heading over the message is a text of the notice, no level of the page; where a page section needs a heading, that is a titolo.
